title: Pendulum

caveats: stylized cartoon animation rather than real footage, so scale is not calibrated

reference.basis: no object of known real size is visible; scene is a stylized cartoon

slow_motion.evidence: no on-screen text, narration or visual effect indicates slow motion

subjects.description: small green round bob hanging from a black string under a dark support

observation.what_happens: A small green ball suspended by a string swings back and forth beneath a dark horizontal support. It moves left and right in a small pendulum arc in the center of the frame, continuing to oscillate for the whole clip.

calibration.note: no ruler needed: the swing is measured as an angle

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth): hold g fixed and measure the pendulum's length L in metres from its swing
reasoning: Theta is a ~0.15 rad sinusoid with period ~1.17 s and slow amplitude decay, and the path is a clean circular arc, so length from g and period is ~0.34 m. Candidates keep exact sin(theta) and g fixed and compete undamped vs linear viscous damping vs quadratic aerodynamic drag to explain the decay into the held-back segment.

Small swing makes linear and quadratic drag look nearly the same.
critique.finding: It swings as a pendulum with length {L} and soft viscous slowing {b}. Its arcs shrink a little each swing yet keep steady timing.
critique.headline: Green ball pendulum swings on, gently losing energy
critique.why_it_won: It fades every swing by the same gentle fraction while quadratic drag would fade large swings faster than small ones.

headline: Green ball pendulum swings on, gently losing energy
finding: It swings as a pendulum with length 0.35 ± 1.54e-4 m and soft viscous slowing 0.0792 ± 0.0023 1/s. Its arcs shrink a little each swing yet keep steady timing.

eyeball.law_in_words: Small-angle pendulum period T equals 2 pi times sqrt(L over g), and oscillation amplitude envelope decays exponentially with linear viscous damping rate b.
